target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: Ranking the one off-the-shelf agent dead last treats a missing human safety readout as the only cost while ignoring the cost of the wait; peripheral blasts went 58 to 82% in a month, so every autologous or donor product on your slate loses weeks this marrow doesn't have. Your threatened CRS veto is at least conditional on there being no mitigation plan, which I can live with, because step-up dosing plus tocilizumab defeats it and preferences.json lists no toxicity_vetoes. Concede the phase-1 has zero efficacy readout, but don't let 85% blasts harden that conditional into a real veto before the burden-reduction-first plan is even asked for.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (CROSSCHECK-001) — left unranked
comment: Declining to rank CBX-250 at all makes evidence tier the sole axis and drops the time axis entirely; for a marrow climbing 58 to 82% in a month, the off-the-shelf option with no manufacturing lag earns a place on the list even below every human-readout pick. Mechanism potency isn't clinical evidence, agreed, but a sub-nanomolar engager with a clean normal-tissue profile (doi:10.1182/blood-2024-201699) is a defensible high-upside bet, not a non-entity. I'll concede the honest limit you're right about: NCT06994676 has zero efficacy or safety readout in a single treated patient.

target_intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning)
comment: Iomab-B at rank 1 is the right call on the evidence: SIERRA is the only randomized phase 3 in the set and durable CR of 17.1% vs 0% (pmid:39298738) is exactly the lever an 85%-blast marrow needs to reach transplant. The OS-null-under-crossover caveat is fair, but for a patient who has no path to cure without getting into HCT2, a durable-CR surrogate that carries active disease across the transplant line is worth backing hard.

target_intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning) — parked off-list
comment: Parking Iomab-B off the ranked list because CD45 radioimmunotherapy isn't NCCN/ELN-adopted lets guideline lag outrank the strongest data point in the dossier; SIERRA is a randomized phase 3 with durable CR 17.1% vs 0% (pmid:39298738) and a go-forward study is open (NCT07157514). Guideline adoption trails evidence by years, and this patient needs the cytoreduction-into-transplant route now, not after the compendium catches up. A trial-route conditioning option with phase-3 backing deserves a rank, not a footnote.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
comment: HCT2 as the curative backbone is fine, but leaning on a 37% 2-year OS from the EBMT related-donor subgroup (pmid:23918951) overstates the footing for a patient who sits in that registry's adverse tail: 85% blasts, MECOM, KMT2A amplification. The favorable ~6-year first remission helps, but this is a retrospective registry, not a reason to slow-walk the faster on-axis levers while the transplant is still weeks of cytoreduction away.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: CBX-250 at rank 1 is the call I'd make too: it is squarely on the stated HLA-A*02:01 axis (preferences.json names HLA-restricted immunotherapy as the reason for the run), recruiting, off-the-shelf, and prior-HCT is permitted at 60 days. For an 85%-blast marrow with no cell-manufacturing wait, that speed edge over the TCR-T handles is the whole argument, and you named the phase-1/no-efficacy caveat honestly.

target_intervention_label: HA-1 / HA-2-directed donor TCR-T after second allo-HCT (Bleakley platform)
comment: Ranking HA-1 TCR-T second is defensible on the 4/9 CR precedent (pmid:38683966), but it inherits the HCT2 timeline plus a three-part gate (A*02:01, recipient-positive/donor-negative HA-1, sorted-CD34 chimerism), none genotyped in patient or sibling. For this pace of relapse I'd flag it more sharply as the slow lever: real cure story, but it can't touch the marrow that's climbing now.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: This acts on the conditional I pre-stated in round 1, and the condition is met, so I am issuing the veto rather than restating a worry. CROSSCHECK-001 (nct:NCT06994676) is first-in-human with the MTD/RP2D listed as not yet established, no characterized AE profile in a single treated patient, and no agent-specific CRS step-dose or priming schema anywhere in the dossier; a CD3 engager's cytokine release scales with tumour burden, and 85% marrow blasts with peripheral blasts climbing 58 to 82% is the worst setting to debut an uncharacterized one. The veto is liftable, not absolute: document burden reduction below this threshold first, a step-up dosing schedule, and tocilizumab on-hand monitoring, and I move to dissent, but ranking it first over the cytoreduction backbone with none of that on file is the safety incompatibility I flagged I would stop.

target_intervention_label: CD123-CD33 compound CAR-T (dual-antigen, iCell cCAR, NCT04156256)
comment: A dual CD33/CD123 construct stacks two toxicities I cannot plan against here: CAR-T-grade cytokine release plus on-target myeloablation of normal CD33- and CD123-positive progenitors, and the supporting data (pmid:29515236) are xenograft-only with no post-allo-HCT human experience. In a re-transplant candidate whose cardiac and organ-function reserve is undocumented, there is no clinical toxicity table to build a management algorithm from. Survival curves in four mouse models do not tell me how to manage marrow aplasia or CRS in this patient, so it does not clear the bar for a ranked slot.

target_intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632, CD123 ADC) monotherapy
comment: You ranked this last and named the veno-occlusive-disease signal yourself, so this is a sequencing caveat, not a fight: VOD was a dose-limiting toxicity (2 of 68) with a 1% treatment-related death against a 21% ORR (pmid:38423051), which is the wrong hepatic risk to carry into a planned HCT2. Gemtuzumab fills the same CD33/CD123-adjacent bridging role with 20-plus years of VOD-surveillance and fractionated-dosing algorithm behind it. Hold the ADC behind the on-label handle until organ-function data land.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager; CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676)
comment: Same acted-on conditional as against risktaker: you ranked CBX-250 first on the primary axis, and a first-in-human CD3 engager with no established MTD (nct:NCT06994676) and no characterized AE profile, delivered to an 85%-blast marrow where cytokine release scales with burden, is the safety incompatibility I pre-stated I would stop. I hear that off-the-shelf speed is the case for it, but speed into an uncharacterized engager at peak burden cuts the wrong way on toxicity. The veto lifts to a dissent the moment a documented CRS-mitigation plan exists for this setting: burden reduced below threshold first, step-up dosing, tocilizumab availability; none is on file, so the stop stands.

target_intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (CD123 ADC) as cytoreductive bridge to HCT2 / cellular consolidation
comment: The bridging logic is sound and you flagged the VOD signal, so my caveat is only about sequencing under a transplant plan: reversible VOD was a dose-limiting toxicity (2 of 68) with a 1% treatment-related death at a 21% ORR (pmid:38423051), and that hepatic risk lands squarely in the peri-HCT2 window. Gemtuzumab covers the same cytoreductive-bridge role with a mature VOD-surveillance and fractionated-dosing playbook. Given a second transplant ahead, I would run the on-label CD33 handle before this ADC until fitness and organ-function data are in.

target_intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC)
comment: We agree this is the on-label floor and I rank it similarly, so my caveat is narrow: the calicheamicin VOD you name is the black-box class risk, and it lands in the peri-HCT2 window this patient is heading toward. The per-grade picture is otherwise reassuring and worth stating (pmid:11432892: G>=3 hyperbilirubinemia 23%, transaminase 17%, no cardiotoxicity), which is exactly why the VOD mitigation cannot stay implicit. Fractionated dosing, VOD surveillance, and defibrotide availability are mandatory conditions on this pick, not optional add-ons.

target_intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab, anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning)
comment: On the evidence I am with you that this is the strongest row, and the number I weight most is the grade >=3 treatment-related AE parity (pmid:39298738: 59.7% vs 59.2%), which says the targeted conditioning did not stack net high-grade toxicity onto conventional care. Where I hold back is load-bearing: SIERRA conditioned first-transplant patients, and choosing conditioning intensity for an HCT2 in someone with no cardiac, hepatic, or renal workup is the unverified safety step. Endorse the tolerability signal; the go/no-go stays contingent on a documented fitness assessment.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager targeting CG1/HLA-A*02:01)
comment: You placed this at rank 4 behind the cytoreduction backbone rather than front-line, so this is a dissent and not the veto I am issuing against the rank-1 nominations. My point is that the 'enroll in a trial' guideline fit carries no safety datum: CROSSCHECK-001 (nct:NCT06994676) has no established MTD and no characterized AE profile, and a CD3 engager's cytokine release scales with the 85%-blast burden. Keep the CRS-in-high-burden gap explicit alongside the enrollment logic, and hold it behind burden reduction plus a documented step-dose and tocilizumab plan, which is the same threshold underneath my veto.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
comment: We both rank HCT2 first, so my caveat is specific to how it is delivered: the ELN/NCCN endorsement you cite is explicitly conditioned on fitness, and non-relapse mortality in a second allograft turns on cardiac, hepatic, and renal reserve that has not been measured in this patient. The Christopeit registry (pmid:23918951) gives ~37% 2-year OS in the related-donor subgroup but no per-term NRM breakdown, and transplanting into 85% blasts sits in the adverse tail of that curve, not the middle. Guideline-consistent, but the fitness gate and cytoreduction-first step stay open before this is deliverable.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: Ranking this first inverts the evidence hierarchy: everything under it is preclinical, and the one supporting row (DOI 10.1182/blood-2024-201699) is an ASH 2024 trial-in-progress-adjacent abstract with no PMID, no per-arm n, and a DOI the dossier itself could not verify and left fail-closed. CROSSCHECK-001 (NCT06994676) has zero human efficacy or safety readout, so a sub-nanomolar EC50 and a PDX survival curve at 0.005 mg/kg tell you the molecule engages the target, not that it helps a patient. The speed argument is real and I will grant it as a tie-breaker among equally unproven off-the-shelf options, but speed is not a reason to seat it above Iomab-B, which actually has a randomized readout in this exact debulk-into-transplant problem.

target_intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform / TSC-100 class), post-HCT
comment: The 4/9 CR you cite (PMID 38683966, ROBINS-I Serious) is a feasibility and safety cohort of nine, not an efficacy estimate a decision can lean on, and I could not retrieve its per-term AE table to even confirm the safety half. A CR proportion off nine patients has an interval wide enough to contain both a real effect and near-nothing, so 'durable HCT2-consolidating immunity' is a hope, not a result. Ranking it third above the xenograft-only cCAR is defensible on maturity grounds; presenting the 4/9 as if it sizes the upside is not.

target_intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586, Y220C-selective p53 reactivator) + venetoclax
comment: The 30% figure you quote is not in the source: PYNNACLE (PMID 41740031, NEJM) reports ORR 20% in solid tumors, all responders KRAS-wild-type, and zero myeloid patients. Ranking it sixth-to-last is the right instinct, but the number attached to the rationale drifts from the paper and the myeloid trial NCT06616636 has no results at all, so this is cross-tumor extrapolation behind a double biomarker gate (confirm TP53 aberration, then confirm Y220C), not a 30%-response bet.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager; CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676)
comment: Preference fit is genuine here and I do not contest that the patient asked for an A*02:01-restricted trial they can travel for. But 'closest match to what the patient asked for' is a preference argument doing the work an evidence argument should do: CBX-250 is first-in-human with no efficacy or safety readout, and the only data are a fail-closed ASH 2024 abstract (DOI 10.1182/blood-2024-201699, no PMID). Off-the-shelf logistics is a fair tie-breaker, not grounds to rank it above Iomab-B (PMID 39298738) or the HA-1 precedent that at least have human readouts; the strongest honest framing is 'preference-matched fastest-to-open trial,' not 'rank 1.'

target_intervention_label: WT1 HLA-A*02:01 TCR-T (WT1-TCRc4 / FH-WT1-E50)
comment: The '100% relapse-free' read from Chapuis (PMID 31235963, n=12) is a prophylaxis cohort infused post-HCT to prevent relapse, against a historical/concurrent comparator, so the survival contrast is confounded and does not transfer to an 85%-blast active relapse. You flag the disease-state mismatch in your own concern line, which I credit, but the effect it implies is relapse-prevention in a selected low-burden setting, not salvage. Keeping it as an allele-contingent lever is reasonable; the n=12 prophylaxis number should not be read as active-disease efficacy.

target_intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (CD123 ADC) as cytoreductive bridge
comment: The ORR 21% is real single-arm activity (PMID 38423051, ROBINS-I Serious) but it comes off the n=29 RP2D expansion, a single-arm surrogate with no comparator, and the response depth is modest for a bridge you are asking to debulk an 85%-blast marrow. It is a more honest cytoreduction lever than the preclinical picks, so as a bridge I do not object to its placement; I would just not let 21% ORR from 29 patients carry more weight than that interval supports, and the VOD signal peri-HCT2 is a real cost against it.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
comment: I agree HCT2 belongs near the top, but the ~37% 2-year OS you lean on comes from a retrospective EBMT registry (PMID 23918951, ROBINS-I Serious), and who gets a second transplant is selected on fitness and disease control, so that number is confounding-by-indication-inflated, not a clean expectation. The ELN 2022 and NCCN 2A framing is expert consensus resting on this same registry tier, not RCT-grade evidence, and it is explicit that the recommendation is conditioned on cytoreduction first, which is the unsolved step in an 85%-blast marrow. The favorable ~6-year first remission helps, but this patient's active high-burden disease is the adverse tail of that 37%, not its middle.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager targeting CG1/HLA-A*02:01)
comment: Rank 4 is far more defensible than the rank-1 the risktaker and advocate gave it, and I credit that you seated it below the on-label and platform picks. The one thing I would tighten: the 'enroll in a trial' preference in NCCN/ELN is category-agnostic and attaches to any open trial, so it supports enrollment as an activity, not CBX-250 as an agent, which has no consensus category and no human readout (NCT06994676, ASH 2024 abstract only). The guideline language should not be allowed to launder a first-in-human asset into looking guideline-backed.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: This is the right call and for the right reason: you ranked it last because the missing datum is a human safety readout, and there is none (NCT06994676 first-in-human, no MTD, no AE profile, ASH 2024 abstract only). I would add the evidence-quality mirror of your toxicity point, that the preclinical strength does not offset the absence of any clinical confirmation, and I share your view that a rank-1 nomination over the transplant backbone inverts the hierarchy. Your conditional CRS veto is well-placed given CRS scales with the 85%-blast burden.

target_intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC)
comment: The 20-year post-marketing safety record is a fair basis for a toxicity-first ranking, but on efficacy the ~30% remission comes from a pooled single-arm phase 2 in CD33+ FIRST relapse with no antecedent haematologic disorder (PMID 11432892, ROBINS-I Serious), a less pretreated population than this FLAG-IDA/venetoclax-refractory patient with extramedullary disease. CR+CRp is a surrogate with no comparator, and single-arm ADC response tracks antigen density that here is still only qualitative. So it is a predictable cytoreduction lever, but expect below 30% and gate it on quantitative CD33 flow before committing.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: Both NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022 do prefer trial enrollment in R/R AML, so CBX-250 is guideline-consonant as an enrollment target, and I keep it on my own list for that. But that preference attaches to the act of enrolling, not to this agent, which is first-in-human with no results and carries no consensus category of its own. Ranking it above the curative backbone that ELN actually names for post-transplant relapse, a second allo-HCT after cytoreduction, treats 'eligible for a phase 1' as if it were the endorsed intervention.

target_intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning)
comment: SIERRA (pmid:39298738) is real randomized data, but CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning is not adopted in NCCN AML v3.2026 or ELN 2022, and the FDA judged SIERRA insufficient for a BLA in 2024 and asked for a fresh non-crossover study, which is the go-forward trial risktaker cites (NCT07157514). So this belongs in the same bucket as CBX-250 for me: a trial-route platform option, not a consensus-endorsed conditioning regimen. Calling it 'randomized evidence behind it' is fair on the trial and misleading on its guideline standing.

target_intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586, Y220C-selective p53 reactivator) + venetoclax
comment: Rezatapopt sits outside guideline-endorsed use on every axis I track: no NCCN or ELN listing, all response data in solid tumors (pmid:41740031), and the myeloid trial (NCT06616636) has posted nothing. It is also doubly contingent, needing TP53 confirmed and then Y220C confirmed, neither resolved. Ranking it at all, even at six, reads as mechanism plausibility standing in for consensus, which is exactly the substitution my prior disfavors.

target_intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT (HCT2) for relapse after first allo-HCT
comment: I ranked this first for the same reason, so this is a concession, not a critique. ELN 2022 centers a second allo-HCT in curative-intent management of post-transplant relapse, NCCN AML v3.2026 keeps it as a category 2A option for fit patients, and the ~6-year first remission puts her on the favorable side of the EBMT related-donor curve (pmid:23918951). The one place we fully agree that matters: the guideline recommendation is conditioned on cytoreduction first, so transplanting into 85% blasts is off-protocol until the marrow is brought down.

target_intervention_label: Iomab-B (131I-apamistamab, anti-CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning)
comment: The critic's evidence-quality read on SIERRA is sound, and I share the surrogate/OS-null-under-crossover caveat. My addition is a guideline-fit one the ranking misses: being the sole randomized phase 3 in the set does not make Iomab-B the consensus choice, because neither NCCN AML v3.2026 nor ELN 2022 has adopted CD45 radioimmunotherapy conditioning, and the FDA declined the SIERRA package as a BLA basis. Rank-1 on trial tier overstates where this sits in practice.

target_intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (Mylotarg, CD33 ADC)
comment: The critic dings gemtuzumab as a single-arm surrogate (pmid:11432892) and ranks it below two registry backbones, which reads the raw evidence tier correctly but skips a layer. NCCN AML v3.2026 lists single-agent gemtuzumab as category 2A for CD33-positive R/R AML: the panel saw the same modest single-arm data the critic is reading and still reached uniform consensus to recommend it, which is what a 2A designation encodes. It is the only on-label, guideline-listed drug on the whole slate, and that standing is worth more than its RoB label alone suggests.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager; CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: The advocate's preference-fit case for CBX-250 is coherent on its own terms, and I agree that enrolling on an A*02:01 trial is the guideline-preferred route in R/R AML under NCCN AML v3.2026 and ELN 2022. Where I split: that preference endorses trial participation, not this specific first-in-human agent, which has no results and no consensus category (NCT06994676). Placing it at rank 1 over the curative backbone lets 'closest to what the patient asked for' outrank 'what the guideline actually endorses for this relapse setting.'

target_intervention_label: WT1 HLA-A*02:01 TCR-T (WT1-TCRc4 / FH-WT1-E50)
comment: Keeping WT1 TCR-T alive as a fallback allele-lever is reasonable trial hygiene, and I do not object to typing A*02:01 and A*24:02 in parallel. The guideline caveat: the Chapuis evidence (pmid:31235963) is post-transplant prophylaxis/MRD, not active-relapse salvage, so even as a trial option it is being proposed outside the disease state where it has data, on top of no NCCN/ELN listing. That is a further stretch than the HA-1 handle, which at least has a relapse-setting readout.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: Leaving CBX-250 off the ranked list entirely answers an evidence-maturity question, not the patient's: free_text names HLA-A*02:01-restricted immunotherapy as the explicit reason for the run, and this is the one on-axis option that is off-the-shelf, recruiting now (NCT06994676), and permits prior allo-HCT after 60 days. I grant the phase-1-no-efficacy reality and that mechanism elegance is not a survival readout. But the workup that unlocks it, HLA-A*02:01 typing, is the same fast records pull the whole axis needs, so it deserves a place in the ranking rather than exclusion.

target_intervention_label: HA-1-specific CD8+/CD4+ TCR-T (Bleakley platform)
comment: Ranking the HA-1 TCR-T last on n=9 maturity is defensible on your axis, but it is the literal handle the case was submitted for, so from the patient's lens it should read as 'gated, not disfavored.' The 4/9 CR with 0 DLTs (pmid:38683966) is thin but sits on exactly the post-HCT relapse setting the run targets, and the gate is genotyping the patient and sibling, not a toxicity or access wall. I would keep it in-frame as a live pathway pending HA-1/HA-2 typing rather than let the maturity rank imply it is off the table.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: Ranking CBX-250 last and threatening a CRS veto de-prioritizes the exact axis the patient came for, and toxicity_vetoes is empty, so there is no stated veto to lean on. I fully concede your load-bearing condition: a CRS-mitigation plan (step-up dosing, tocilizumab on hand, cytoreduction to lower the 85%-blast burden first) has to be documented before this moves, and the phase-1 no-efficacy status is real. But 'no characterized CRS profile yet' is an argument to make the mitigation plan a gate, not to bury an off-the-shelf, recruiting on-axis trial (NCT06994676) beneath cytoreduction options the patient did not prioritize.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager targeting CG1/HLA-A*02:01)
comment: You correctly credit CBX-250 with the NCCN/ELN 'enroll in a trial' preference, but ranking it fourth behind gemtuzumab undersells the patient's own framing: prefers_trials is true, travel is acceptable, and this is the on-axis A*02:01 trial that is off-the-shelf and recruiting (NCT06994676). Your own logic that enrollment is the preferred R/R route argues for lifting it above an on-label cytoreductive bridge that is not the reason for this run. I would keep gemtuzumab as the available fallback and let the recruiting on-axis trial sit higher on preference grounds, with the pending HLA-A*02:01 typing as the honest gate.

target_intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic CG1/HLA-A*02:01 bispecific T-cell engager, CROSSCHECK-001)
comment: Rank-1 CBX-250 lands on the patient's stated axis: HLA-A*02:01-restricted immunotherapy, curative intent, trials acceptable including travel, no toxicity or modality veto to trip. Your off-the-shelf-speed rationale for the 85%-blast marrow tracks the trial row (recruiting, prior allo-HCT permitted after 60 days, NCT06994676), and you name the phase-1 CRS caveat honestly rather than hiding it. One preference-lens note: the HA-1 TCR-T at your rank 3 is the literal reason the case was submitted, so I would keep it visibly close behind, not below two non-axis picks.
